svg.aria-label: How the agent-orchestration framework works: price data becomes point-in-time features, 498 stock agents each form an independent opinion and then revise it after reading peers routed through a configurable communication graph, a manager agent turns the final opinions into a dollar-neutral long-short book, and evaluation grades it on out-of-sample forward returns that never enter a prompt.
svg.title: Agent Orchestration — framework overview

g.text: One LLM agent per S&P-500 firm forms an independent view, revises it after reading peers routed over a configurable graph, and a manager turns the result into a long/short book.
Research question — does letting the agents talk produce a better book than the same agents working alone?
forward returns t → t+H · reach evaluation.py directly and never appear in any prompt
the dual-brain pattern — an LLM path with a rule twin behind it
who reads whom, and when the shared world is allowed to move
all 498 final opinions → one dollar-neutral book
one stock's brief — 10 features as cross-sectional percentiles
+ inbox: the peer messages this topology lets it read
ticker · score 0–100 · direction · confidence · thesis ≤ 50 words · round
The rule twin is built before the model is ever called, at every call site.
Measured on the 32-day run: 76 fallbacks in 111,552 calls (0.07%).
All 498 revisions are computed off the SAME snapshot, then
posted together. Posting as you go would let the last agent in
dict order react to a world the first one never saw.
N_ROUNDS = 2 revision rounds run per rebalance date.
BatchScheduler fires a whole round's prompts at once — inside a round
the agents are independent, so batching changes no result.
candidates() — a shortlist, not the table
Rank all 498 by score, then show the manager only the
top 30 and bottom 30 — the full table runs ≈12k tokens
against a 4,096 context, so every call would fail.
· a pick is off the shortlist
· one side is empty — that is a
long weights sum to +1 · short weights to −1 · gross 2 · net 0
BOOK_SIZING = "flexible": the manager chooses its own count per side,
inside [5, 50], instead of a hard-wired top-5 / bottom-5.
03 — THE EXPERIMENTAL VARIABLE: WHO HEARS WHOM
Same ten agents, same ring, in every panel — only the edges change. Each agent still scores only its own stock; the graph decides whose score it may read before revising.

Degree and structure are confounded today (full = 497 peers, sector ≈ 54, sparse ≈ 50, corr_topk = 10), so any structural claim needs the two controls in TOPOLOGY_PLAN.md §3: a degree-matched random graph, and a peer-shuffling placebo.

A second tier exists in hierarchy.py — one industry leader per sector aggregates its members and the leaders then form their own council — but it has not been run against a model yet, so it is left off this picture.
Features at date t read prices ≤ t only.
Forward returns go straight to evaluation.py — no
prompt has ever seen one. The backtest window opens
A run never dies on a bad generation
Every LLM call site precomputes its rule twin.
Unparseable JSON, a non-numeric score, a ticker off
the shortlist, a one-sided book — each falls back and
continues; _count_fallbacks() logs the rate per round.
Every run states its own cost
tokens, wall time, latency percentiles and fallbacks
per (date, topology, round), then projects the full
date range. Exact vs estimated is always labelled.
